text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the CT images we just reviewed, what specific symptoms are you experiencing in your legs, such as swelling, or do you have any history of blood clots or recent long travel? Also, have you noticed any vaginal bleeding or irregular periods?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Carcinoma causing Superior Vena Cava Syndrome (SVCS).

The patient presents with the classic triad of ovarian malignancy (abdominal girth, dyspnea, fatigue) with normal CA-125, suggesting a mucinous, germ cell, or epithelial subtype; the acute onset of shortness of breath requires immediate evaluation for SVC obstruction secondary to retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy compressing the mediastinal veins.
